Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: Eswatini's Data Protection Act includes breach notification obligations: the law requires data controllers to notify the Commission and data subjects in the event of an unauthorised data security breach (mandatory breach notification).
revision_notes: Sources verified: dataprotection.africa summary and ESCCOM mandate page confirm mandatory breach notification under section 17 of the Data Protection Act, 2022. Cross-checked against the Eswatini Data Protection Authority (EDPA) website, which specifies a 72-hour notification window from the controller becoming aware of a breach, and against a 2024 EDPA enforcement notice issued against Liberty Life Swaziland for failure to notify a data compromise, confirming active enforcement of the requirement. Score of 3 (Mandatory) is well supported and confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Eswatini's Data Protection Act, 2022, in force since 4 March 2022, makes breach notification mandatory. Under section 17, a data controller must notify the Eswatini Data Protection Authority (EDPA) and affected data subjects as soon as reasonably possible after discovering that personal information has been accessed or acquired by an unauthorised person, and the EDPA requires notification within 72 hours of the controller becoming aware of a breach. The Authority actively enforces this obligation, having issued a formal enforcement notice against a financial services provider in 2024 for failing to notify affected data subjects of a breach.

Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: Eswatini has a comprehensive Data Protection Act (No.5 of 2022) in force (from 4 March 2022) providing general personal data protection across sectors (public/private).
revision_notes: Sources verified: dataprotection.africa and the ESCCOM mandate page confirm the Data Protection Act, 2022 is a general, cross-sectoral personal-data law applying to all data controllers and processors, including payment service providers. No payment-specific data provisions were found in the Act text or on the EDPA website, so code 2 (General Data Protection Legislation) rather than 3 (Specific Payment Data Provisions) is correct. Confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Eswatini has a comprehensive, general-purpose Data Protection Act, 2022, in force since 4 March 2022, which applies across public and private sectors, including payment service providers, but does not contain provisions specific to payment transaction data. The Act is administered and enforced by the Eswatini Data Protection Authority (formerly the Eswatini Communications Commission's data protection mandate).
